concept.centerRule: Keep every Spirit occurrence attached to its Scripture referent, speaker, verb, recipient, and setting; recurrence can be traced, but divine, human, dispositional, life-and-death, prophetic, angelic, and demonic uses may never be silently equated.

characterAnchors.label: God / the LORD
characterAnchors.note: Creates, gives, puts within, pours, sends, speaks, leads, and is named through Spirit language in distinct sources.

characterAnchors.label: Jesus
characterAnchors.note: Is conceived by, anointed with, full of, led by, and speaks about the Holy Spirit in the Gospel witnesses.

characterAnchors.label: Prophets and speakers
characterAnchors.note: Speak, testify, prophesy, and are moved in sources that explicitly name Spirit action.

characterAnchors.label: Disciples and communities
characterAnchors.note: Receive, are filled, worship, pray, discern, bear fruit, and are addressed in Spirit language.

characterAnchors.label: Other spirits
characterAnchors.note: Unclean, evil, deceiving, angelic, and human spirits remain textually distinguished from God’s Spirit.

concept.throughline: Spirit language begins over creation, enters accounts of life and death, inward condition, skilled work, leadership, prophecy, promise, Jesus’ identity and mission, the communities’ worship and conduct, discernment among spirits, and Revelation’s visions and invitation.

dissects.posture: Read Revelation 22:15–19 as evidence about the Spirit, keeping its action, claim, context, and limits distinct.
dissects.tension: The passage states revelation 22:15–19 names God’s Spirit within a source unit where the Spirit invites; the wording centers attention on “The Spirit and the bride say.” It does not by itself supply every cause or later interpretation of this part of the Spirit.
